title: Weekly impact hypotheses log — Ramya
body:
Quick note: using this doc as a lightweight lab notebook for 2-week experiments aimed at increasing shipping velocity and measurable impact in Q1. Not all items are polished — rough hypotheses, small experiments, and daily micro-retros. Update at least twice a week.

Context: role = senior software engineer, focus = kernel selection + batching heuristics for the serving runtime. My goal is to move beyond tactical PRs and deliver repeatable playbooks that others can adopt. Emphasis on small, measurable bets rather than big unvalidated plans.

Personal objectives (3):
- Obj A: Increase production throughput impact for small-sequence workloads.
  - KR A1: Reduce average per-token GPU time for 8-32 token sequences by 12% on p4x nodes (baseline = 1.45 ms/token).
  - KR A2: Ship 2 platform-facing optimizations with rollout docs and perf tests.
- Obj B: Improve team knowledge sharing and reduce onboarding time for runtime heuristics.
  - KR B1: Create 1 reproducible tutorial notebook + 1 short internal talk (20 min).
  - KR B2: Pair-program with 3 engineers to land infra changes; collect feedback.
- Obj C: Carve weekly deep-focus time to unblock big-ticket work.
  - KR C1: Protect two 3-hour focus blocks per week for at least 8/10 working weeks.

Weekly hypotheses & experiments (working list):
1) Hypothesis: Adding a tiny adaptive prefix cache for recent KV pairs will cut repeated-short-request cost without hurting tail latency.
   Signal: % of requests hitting prefix cache; 95th percentile latency remains within SLA (+10% allowed).
   Experiment: Implement cache in branch, enable for 10% traffic via canary route SRV-4125, compare cost per token and tail latency for 2 weeks.
   Confidence: 3/5
   Notes: ask SRE (Ivy) about observability hooks for the canary.

2) Hypothesis: A heuristic to favor faster GEMM kernels for seq_len<=32 can reduce token time by ~10% but may regress at seq_len>=512.
   Signal: mean token time by sequence bucket; regression surface table.
   Experiment: Add a scoring function for kernel choice, run full model bench across seq buckets, and gate with perf test in CI.
   Confidence: 4/5
   Linked: GH PR/287 is the starting patch.

3) Hypothesis: Weekly 30-minute office-hours for runtime Q&A will increase peer adoption of batching patterns and reduce low-quality PRs.
   Signal: number of PRs needing rework on perf tests, attendance and follow-up actions.
   Experiment: host 4 sessions, measure PR outcomes and gather quick survey.
   Confidence: 4/5

Two-week running log (notes-to-self and short diary):
- 2025-01-06: Kickoff. Baselines captured: small-seq baseline 1.45 ms/token on p4x; CI perf flakiness noted. TODO: stabilize perf CI before canary.
- 2025-01-09: Quick spike: implemented cache prototype (in-memory map keyed by request prefix). Microbench shows 8% gain on contrived workload. Need end-to-end metrics.
- 2025-01-11: Paused due to CI noise. Talked with Eliot about deterministic workload harness. Action: add seed control and synthetic traces.
- 2025-01-15: Bench harness stable. Canary setup doc started. Scheduled canary cut for 2025-01-21.
- 2025-01-21: Enabled cache for 10% in eu-west. Early telemetry: cache hit 18% on experimental cohort, mean token time down 6%, 95th latency +4% (within tolerated slack).
- 2025-01-24: Chat with Ivy — want extra tracing for KV lifecycle. Added simple event markers.
- 2025-01-28: Midpoint review: cost per token down ~5% in canary, but tail latency spikes correlate with memory GC at certain workloads. Hypothesis: garbage accumulation in cache eviction.
- 2025-02-03: Implemented bounded LRU with backpressure flag; re-deployed; tail improved.
- 2025-02-14: Ran kernel-selection bench across seq buckets — decision table built. Found a 14% win on 8-24 bucket using alternative GEMM kernel.
- 2025-02-20: Delivered the short internal talk (recorded) and dropped the tutorial notebook link in #serving-runtime. Positive feedback, 3 follow-up pairing requests.

Retrospective notes (what worked / didn't):
- Wins: shipping small, fast experiments and coupling them to clear signals helped momentum. The canary approach with limited blast radius worked well.
- Pain: perf CI flakiness stole 2 days; need a stable harness and better synthetic seeds before future canaries.
- Surprise: small-seq optimization unlocked downstream cost wins for several small customers; need to add to customer notes in the console.

Open questions / risks:
- How will cache interact with preemption and multi-tenancy on Dedicated pools? (flag as research item).
- Do we need to expose cache control in per-customer routing policy?
- Is the kernel-selection table maintainable as new architectures (H100, next-gen) arrive?

Action items (next):
- [ ] Finalize canary playbook and postmortem template (owner: Ramya) — due 2025-03-03.
- [ ] Add deterministic seeds to perf CI and document (owner: Eliot).
- [ ] Pair with Mikael to generalize kernel scoring into plugin-style config (owner: Ramya/Mikael).
- [ ] Run a short user-impact sweep with Solutions Eng to identify customers benefiting from small-seq wins.

Notes to self: keep experiments < 2 weeks; write one-line summary after each deploy; keep the telemetry simple — prefer a single metric you can explain in a meeting.

Draft blurb for 1:1 / skip-level: "This sprint I validated two light-touch runtime changes that reduced per-token cost for short sequences by ~5–12% in canaries; next steps are to stabilize perf CI and generalize kernel selection. I want to protect 6 hours/wk for deep work to land the follow-ups."

Meta: store follow-up artifacts under /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/experiments/ramya/ (TODO: move notebooks and perf-captures there).

End of doc (update cadence: Mon/Wed/Friday).
